presentingComplaint: Progressive drowsiness and cold, unresponsive state over 5 days
history: Brought to ED in mid-winter by her daughter after becoming increasingly slow, mumbling and finally barely rousable at home. Known moderate COPD (ex-smoker, on inhaled LABA/ICS, one prior admission for exacerbation) and hypertension. Also has hypothyroidism following radioiodine ablation for Graves' disease 8 years ago, maintained on levothyroxine 100 mcg daily — but the daughter reports the prescription lapsed about 10 weeks ago and her mother 'kept meaning to refill it'. Over the past fortnight she was constipated, off her food, complained of feeling cold even indoors, and her voice had become gruff. No fever, cough or increased sputum. No chest pain. The ED team initially considered a COPD exacerbation with CO2 narcosis given her hypercapnia and drowsiness.
examination: Obtunded, GCS 9 (E2V2M5), responds only to painful stimuli. Cool, dry, coarse skin with non-pitting periorbital and pretibial puffiness. Macroglossia and hoarse, gravelly voice noted before deterioration. Chest with mildly prolonged expiration and scattered rhonchi but no focal crepitations or bronchial breathing. Heart sounds soft, no murmur, JVP not raised. Abdomen soft, sluggish bowel sounds. Neurologically: markedly delayed (hung-up) relaxation of the ankle reflexes; no focal deficit, no neck stiffness. Core temperature measured with a low-reading thermometer.

labs.abg: pH 7.29, PaCO2 68 mmHg, PaO2 58 mmHg, HCO3 30 (chronic + acute hypercapnia)

imaging: Chest radiograph: hyperinflation consistent with known COPD, small cardiac-silhouette effusion possible, no consolidation. ECG: sinus bradycardia at 44/min with low-voltage QRS and prolonged QT.
microbiology: Blood cultures sent and subsequently negative; no infective focus identified. Urinalysis bland.
differentialDiagnoses: Myxoedema coma precipitated by levothyroxine non-adherence and cold exposure
COPD exacerbation with hypercapnic CO2 narcosis (confounding comorbidity)
finalDiagnosis: Myxoedema coma (decompensated hypothyroidism) in a patient with confounding COPD-related hypercapnia
citations: American Thyroid Association — Guidelines for the Treatment of Hypothyroidism in Adults (2014)
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Hypothyroidism and Myxedema Coma
stewardship: Non-infective decompensation; no empiric antibiotics indicated once cultures and imaging exclude a source. Treat with IV levothyroxine (loading dose) ± liothyronine, IV hydrocortisone until coexisting adrenal insufficiency is excluded, passive rewarming, cautious correction of hyponatraemia, and ventilatory support for hypercapnia.
contraindications: Avoid aggressive external active rewarming (precipitates vasodilatory shock)
Avoid rapid overcorrection of hyponatraemia (osmotic demyelination risk)
Do not give levothyroxine before hydrocortisone if adrenal insufficiency is possible (may precipitate adrenal crisis)
Sedatives/opioids worsen hypoventilation and CO2 narcosis
edgeCases: COPD-related chronic hypercapnia can mask the diagnosis by attributing drowsiness to CO2 narcosis
Precipitants (infection, cold, sedatives, missed levothyroxine) frequently coexist and must be sought
Hypothermia and bradycardia may be wrongly attributed to sepsis or primary cardiac disease
expectedMaiK: Decompensated hypothyroidism (myxoedema coma) triggered by 10 weeks of levothyroxine non-adherence and cold exposure — hypothermia, bradycardia, hypoventilation, altered sensorium, non-pitting oedema, delayed reflexes, hyponatraemia, raised CK and markedly elevated TSH with very low free T4 — with COPD hypercapnia as a confounding overlap.
expectedNextQuestions: When was levothyroxine last taken and why was it stopped?
Any recent infection, sedative/opioid use, or cold exposure as a precipitant?
History of thyroid surgery, radioiodine, or neck irradiation?
Baseline functional status and prior COPD blood-gas values?
expectedInvestigations: TSH and free T4 (and free T3)
Random cortisol (± short Synacthen) before/with steroid cover
Septic screen to exclude precipitant (cultures, CXR)
regressionAssertions: Differential should include metabolic_enceph and copd_exac_ni given the confounding hypercapnia
Must recommend TSH/free T4 and random cortisol
Must not recommend empiric antibiotics in the absence of an infective focus
Should flag hydrocortisone before/with levothyroxine and cautious rewarming
